NVDA.headline: Is AMD's Stock in Trouble After a Concerning Short-Seller Report?
NVDA.description: A short-seller report from Hunterbrook Media raised concerns about AMD's exposure to China, claiming over 20% of its revenue comes from Chinese customers and that blacklisted Chinese company IEIT Systems has access to AMD firmware. AMD dismissed the allegations, stating compliance with U.S. export laws. The stock has fallen over 30% from its 52-week high and trades at nearly 100x trailing earnings. While long-term investors may find value, short-term risks remain elevated given the high valuatio

NVDA.headline: Is the Worst Over for Nvidia Stock?
NVDA.description: Nvidia raised fiscal 2028 guidance and reported strong Q3 results with 103% revenue growth to $115.8B, exceeding expectations. CEO Jensen Huang's unexpected reinstatement eased investor concerns. However, the article warns that longer-term risks persist, including increasing competition from ASICs and AMD GPUs, potential margin compression, and the weakening of Nvidia's CUDA moat as AI models improve. Despite trading at an attractive forward P/E below 10x, the analyst recommends staying on the s

NVDA.headline: Nvidia Soared 35% on Jensen Huang's Return. Is It Too Late to Buy?
NVDA.description: Nvidia's stock surged 35% after the board unanimously reinstated CEO Jensen Huang following his resignation two weeks prior. Despite the dramatic personal controversies, the company's fundamentals remain strong with Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion (up 103% YoY) and Q4 guidance of $130 billion. The analyst argues it's not too late to buy, as the stock is still down 11% for the year and the market has priced in more worry than fundamentals warrant.

NVDA.headline: Huang's Nvidia Return Tests a Rule Breaker Trait
NVDA.description: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO after 11 days, causing the stock to surge 30% and recover most losses from his resignation. While the board cited national security clearance and stakeholder interests, key-person risk remains unresolved as Nvidia has no public succession plan. The Rule Breakers team will reassess Nvidia's status in December, with the ongoing foreign intelligence investigation potentially influencing the decision.

NVDA.headline: President Donald Trump Just Took Credit for Jensen Huang’s Return as Nvidia CEO. Is the Trump Put Now Back in Play?
NVDA.description: President Trump claimed credit for convincing Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following his resignation. Huang's return sparked a 30.5% surge in Nvidia stock and broader market gains. The article examines whether a 'Trump put' exists—Trump's willingness to intervene to support the stock market—while noting its limitations given policy challenges and congressional constraints.

NVDA.headline: Is Micron Technology Stock a Buy at $700?
NVDA.description: Micron Technology's stock rallied to $700 following Nvidia's announcement of Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO. While the company showed impressive growth with revenue nearly five times higher year-over-year, the analyst recommends caution due to uncertainty around the memory market cycle and cyclical industry volatility. Despite trading at a low 10x earnings multiple, the stock remains speculative and risky.

NVDA.headline: Is Nvidia Stock Cheap?
NVDA.description: Nvidia stock appears undervalued after dropping 35% from its all-time high, trading at a forward P/E ratio of roughly 10. CEO Jensen Huang's return to leadership strengthens investor confidence in the company's guidance. With 103% year-over-year revenue growth, retained customer relationships, and a deep backlog, the stock presents a buying opportunity despite recent volatility.

NVDA.headline: Nvidia vs. TSMC: With Jensen Huang Back, Which AI Stock Is the Better Buy for 2027?
NVDA.description: Following semiconductor industry volatility, the article compares Nvidia and TSMC as AI investment opportunities for 2027. Nvidia is favored due to its dominant market position in AI processors, exceptional profitability (62.5% net margin), stronger growth (93.3% YoY), and more attractive valuation (13x forward P/E vs TSMC's 19.3x). NVDA.headline: Trump Wants Elon Musk on His Side. Democrats May Have Just Given Him a Reason to Look Across the Aisle.
NVDA.description: Elon Musk finds himself in a rare position of being courted by both Republicans and Democrats as his SpaceX plans to deploy one million AI data center satellites. This comes as communities nationwide reject ground-based data centers, making Musk's space-based solution potentially critical infrastructure for both parties' AI ambitions.

NVDA.headline: Anthropic Just Went Public. Here's What Happens to Most IPO Stocks in the First Week.
NVDA.description: Anthropic completed the largest IPO ever, raising close to $120 billion, with its stock jumping 17% on the first day before falling 10% on the second day. Historical data shows IPO stocks gain an average of 19% on their first day but typically underperform the market index by 21% over three years, suggesting investors should wait for the initial hype to subside before buying.

The company expects to reach positive adjusted net income in 2028 as GPU contracts renew and infrastructure expands. The key question is whether operating income growth can outpace financing costs to improve the company's financial outlook.

ASX.headline: Are Computer and Technology Stocks Lagging  ASE Technology (ASX) This Year?
ASX.description: ASE Technology Hldg (ASX) has significantly outperformed the Computer and Technology sector year-to-date, gaining 63.2% compared to the sector's -6.2% decline. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving analyst sentiment, as consensus earnings estimates have risen 8.3% over the past 90 days. Amphenol (APH) is another sector outperformer with a 3.2% year-to-date return and similar positive earnings revision trends.

ASX.headline: LSCC Rides on Balanced Organic & Inorganic Growth: Should You Buy?
ASX.description: Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) reported Q3 revenues of $291 million, up 118.3% year-over-year, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand and FPGA growth. The company's industrial segment revenues rose 34.9%, with expected acceleration to 70% in Q4. The AMI acquisition contributed $39.1 million in Q3 revenues, expanding Lattice's AI server and security capabilities. The stock has gained 43.6% over the past year and holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating.

DELL.description: Dell Technologies is set to report Q3 fiscal 2027 results on November 24 with expected revenues of $49 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $6.50. The company projects $19 billion in AI server revenues supported by a $95 billion backlog. While strong AI infrastructure demand and enterprise modernization drive growth, supply constraints and lower AI server margins pose risks to profitability.

DELL.description: Nvidia, Coherent, and Dell Technologies have all declined significantly from their record highs (36%, 48%, and 45% respectively), but their underlying businesses remain strong with accelerating data center demand. Despite recent stock weakness, all three companies show robust growth metrics and attractive valuations, making them potential long-term buys through 2030.

SKHY.headline: Nvidia Without Jensen Huang: 3 Things That Could Go Right and 3 That Could Go Wrong
SKHY.description: Following Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO amid allegations of affairs, the company faces both opportunities and risks. Positive factors include an intact supply chain moat, continued strong growth forecasted at 75% for fiscal 2028, and potential stock multiple expansion. However, risks include potential deterioration of the SpaceX relationship, slowdown in AI infrastructure investment, and margin compression from increased competition and eroding CUDA moat.

CBRS.description: Cerebras stock surged 19.2% following Nvidia's announcement that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, with Nvidia shares jumping 35.5%. The author suggests that Nvidia's revival is bad news for Cerebras and recommends Nvidia stock over Cerebras based on valuation metrics.

MU.description: Wall Street staged a strong rebound on November 23, with the Nasdaq surging 6.79% and the S&P 500 jumping 5.00% following last week's sell-off. Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO fueled renewed enthusiasm for AI stocks, with Nvidia leading gains at +32.05%. The broader semiconductor sector also rallied, though investors should monitor upcoming inflation data and earnings expectations for sustainability.

MU.headline: Why Nvidia Rehiring Jensen Huang Is Making Micron Stock Skyrocket Today
MU.description: Nvidia announced it has rehired Jensen Huang as CEO after reconsidering his firing, causing Nvidia stock to surge 35%. This positive development boosted investor confidence in AI's future, leading Micron stock to jump 16.5% as investors expect continued GPU sales will drive demand for memory chips. Micron is now viewed as undervalued at 8x trailing earnings with expected 43% annual earnings growth over five years.

MU.headline: Walmart, Target, Anthropic, Amazon, Nvidia, Micron and Alphabet are part of Zacks Earnings Preview
MU.description: Walmart's Q3 results disappointed investors with decelerating comp growth and underwhelming guidance, while Target impressed with strong comps of +5.6%. The broader retail sector shows mixed performance with 75% beating EPS estimates. S&P 500 Q3 earnings are up +28.9% with 82.3% beating estimates, though results excluding Nvidia, Micron, and Alphabet show more modest +21.5% growth. Q4 earnings estimates are tracking at +28.3% growth.

MU.headline: The S&P 500 Just Had Its Worst Week in 18 Months. Is This a Buying Opportunity?
MU.description: The S&P 500 experienced its worst week in 18 months, declining nearly 9% and entering correction territory, primarily driven by a sharp selloff in AI stocks amid concerns about massive infrastructure spending returns and Nvidia's CEO resignation. However, historical data suggests such sharp weekly declines are typically followed by strong rebounds, with the median 12-month return after 5%+ weekly declines reaching 18.8%, making this potentially a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

MU.headline: Prediction: Dec. 9 Will Be a Huge Day for the Stock Market
MU.description: December 9, 2026 is expected to be a major market day with three significant events converging: the FOMC's federal funds rate decision (likely a 25 basis point increase), Broadcom's earnings report as a key AI semiconductor barometer, and Micron's ability to begin its expanded $35.16 billion share repurchase program. Each event could significantly impact stock prices and investor sentiment across the technology and semiconductor sectors.

MU.headline: Where Will Micron Stock Be in 3 Years?
MU.description: Micron Technology's stock has declined significantly in recent months but remains up 120% year-to-date. The article presents three scenarios for the stock's performance over the next three years: a bull case ($1,800-$2,200), a base case ($1,100-$1,400), and a bear case ($400-$600). The analyst predicts the stock will reach the lower end of the base-case range, expecting an 80%+ cumulative gain, contingent on sustained HBM demand and competition from Chinese chipmaker CXMT.

MU.headline: Nvidia Just Delivered Incredible Results. Buy This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Instead If You’re Still Worried About the Semiconductor Giant’s Future
MU.description: Nvidia delivered impressive Q3 results with 103% revenue growth and raised fiscal 2028 guidance to 75%, but concerns about leadership transition persist. The article suggests ASML as an alternative AI investment, as it manufactures the advanced EUV lithography equipment essential for producing cutting-edge chips like Nvidia's Vera Rubin processors. ASML benefits from a diversified customer base including TSMC, Samsung, and Intel, and plans to increase production capacity by 30% in 2027.

MU.description: The article suggests that Micron and Sandisk may be better investment alternatives to Nvidia due to lower valuations and reduced headline risks. MRVL.headline: 3 Millionaire-Maker AI Chip Stocks Wall Street Isn't Talking About
MRVL.description: The article highlights three smaller AI chip stocks with potential for market-beating returns: Marvell Technology, which specializes in ASIC and interconnect chips for data centers; Silicon Motion Technology, a NAND flash controller supplier experiencing explosive growth; and Qualcomm, an established chipmaker entering the AI data center market with major partnerships and a low valuation.
